parsed.explanation: Combined regime pairs federal binary-sex document, visa-fraud and facility restrictions—allowed to take effect by the Supreme Court—with state birth-sex facilities, shelters and prisons, a survived drag-performance felony, and a minor-care ban upheld in 2025. Document mismatch therefore triggers refusal, possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, arrest and birth-sex custody; immigration and prison custody document beatings, sexual abuse and hormone removal. Functioning courts and some injunctions/lawsuits mitigate, but they also enforce upheld hostile laws, and no execution pathway is documented. Universal birth-sex exposure and custody harm place this well below exclusion-only regimes.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal X markers stopped and passports limited to M/F per supporting documents; Supreme Court allowed restrictions in Nov 2025. Passports confiscated/blocked and travellers stranded. Visa cable mandates refusal on document discrepancy and possible permanent fraud ineligibility. State birth-certificate change barred since 1977; 2023 law defines sex by birth anatomy/genetics.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry. Fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, and has limited waivers. Passport-marker litigation is pending; not all states bar marker changes.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate from refusal to material-misrepresentation/fraud analysis, then detention and birth-sex custody.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections model from 2026 mandates short haircuts, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. State 2026 Act mandates birth-sex prison placement. Trespass arrestee was held in men's ward 24 hours.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No capital punishment for gender conduct is documented. Some national orders have been enjoined, and the bathroom-trespass defendant received pretrial release.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility or immigration arrest leads into birth-sex placement, compounding documented custody harm.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Executive order bars federal single-sex facilities congruent with identity. Nine states ban such use in all government buildings; this state’s April 2026 Act requires birth-sex facilities and bars trans women from women's shelters. A 2019 statute defines trans bathroom use matching identity as indecent exposure, frequency not documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Twenty-nine states have no mapped ban in these categories. Criminal trespass requires wilful entry plus refusal to depart after request, with exemptions; warning-sign requirement was struck down.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal binary-sex definition interacts with state facility, shelter, school and prison rules as one universal-exposure system.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care under 18, including out-of-state telehealth, upheld June 2025; national orders target minor care and proposed federal insurance bar. Inmate care is banned and corrections policy removes hormones.
care_services.protection: Several national orders have been blocked or enjoined and health-rule proposals remain challenged. Adult non-custodial care is not documented as banned.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor seeking continuity faces denial; a parent assisting may face state civil penalties, turning care access into legal exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State adult-entertainment law criminalises male/female impersonators where a child could see; first offence up to 11 months 29 days, repeat felony 1–6 years, and it survived appeal. Counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups described as radically pro-transgender; public opinion favours birth-sex documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Drag law was initially found vague/overbroad and a separate suit remains ongoing. Several national orders were enjoined, and signage mandates were struck down.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing supports enforcement of drag, school, facility and document laws despite litigation elsewhere.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor care is banned; schools must out students requesting different names/pronouns to parents; sports use birth-sex proof; teachers face investigation for facilitating social transition. State law adds civil penalties for adults helping minors obtain banned care and regret suits against parents/providers.
minors_guardians.protection: School-bathroom and sports litigation remains ongoing, and some national directives have been enjoined, but no operative visitor-minor protection is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A family seeking schooling, sports or care triggers state reporting, birth-sex placement and potential adult liability.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Dossier reports discrimination, refusal of service and beatings, a 2021 report of officials turning a blind eye, and availability of gay/trans panic defence. The 7.8/100k killing figure is an undercount floor with 10 deaths over 18 years, so it is not used as a rate.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime law covers gender identity; state prosecutor opinion supports enhancement when victim selected because transgender. Raw state recorded counts are 0–2, without denominators or methodology.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State hate-crime statute omits gender identity, weakening local police remedy despite federal coverage and prosecutor guidance.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport restrictions, drag law and minor-care ban are operative; other orders’ effect depends on timing and litigation. Enforcement varies by state and agency, and several visitor outcomes—licence suit, 2026 Act enforcement, drag-law application to trans visitors—are unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation, injunctions, federal employment and hate-crime protections, and occasional successful challenges provide some recourse, though slow and uneven.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Functioning courts both restrain some measures and uphold others; they do not cancel exposures created by operative birth-sex and document rules.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: mandatory birth-sex prison placement and criminalisation connected to gender presentation, brief-to-moderate sentences, no execution. This case adds federal border fraud risk, felony repeat drag penalties and documented immigration-custody sexual abuse, but also stronger litigation/injunction access, keeping it near this level.

Lower: 0.35-A involves routine exclusion and humiliation with no imprisonment. Here imprisonment is legally available, custody includes birth-sex placement and documented abuse, and border mismatch can support lifetime ineligibility, making consequences materially more severe.

Higher: 0.15-B features months of detention, tolerated assaults, withheld care and illusory habeas. This dossier documents serious custody abuse, but courts sometimes enjoin/enforce remedies, pretrial release occurred, and capital punishment for gender conduct is not credibly documented.

parsed.synthesis: The operative system is not a patchwork of isolated rules: binary-sex documents cause border and everyday mismatch; mismatch can trigger refusal, fraud scrutiny, facility trespass or drag-law enforcement; arrest then leads to birth-sex custody, where hormone removal and abuse are documented. State law extends this to shelters, schools and minors’ care, while federal counterterrorism framing and majority support for birth-sex documents reinforce enforcement. Civil-litigation and injunctions are real mitigations, but Supreme Court decisions have kept key passport and care restrictions alive, and the state drag ban is enforceable. That combination—universal exposure, felony liability, hostile custody and no lethal federal pathway—supports a score around 0.27.
